newsitem.title: UK: UK's water watchdog says rate of leaks too high.
newsitem.headline: UK's water watchdog says rate of leaks too high.

text.p: Britain's water industry watchdog Ofwat on Monday said Yorkshire Water was on track to meet targets for cutting leaks but levels of water seeping out of pipes for the industry as a whole were too high.

"The industry's leakage levels are still too high. Spending on leakage control should increase up to the point where to continue would cost the company more than other means to bridge the gap between supply and demand," Ofwat head Ian Byatt said in a statement.

Ofwat was announcing Yorkshire Water's leakage assessment, which it was asked to prepare after a disastrous performance during the hot summer of 1995 when it was forced to bring in water from other areas by tanker.
Byatt said the company, which has since had a management shake-up and improved performance, had fulfilled undertakings over leakage.
He said environmental costs in reducing leakage also had to be taken into account.
Byatt called on water companies to assess economic leakage levels and the costs involved, adding that some had been "too complacent and have sat back waiting for the results of Yorkshire's work."
Yorkshire's report was "not a template for the industry which still has much work to do," he added.
He called for comments on Yorkshire's report and said advice would be required from the Environment Agency, adding that he would set leakage targets for next year for the industry in the autumn.
And he warned that leakage would be an important factor in setting prices at the next review in 1999.

"I will not allow for new resource development in price limits unless I am satisfied that leakage is at an economic level and that demand is being properly managed," Byatt said. -- London Newsroom +44171 542 7717
